subtype: Approach: building a friendly connection first [Action]
passage: Three weeks before the inter-house fest, Damini and Abhinav ended up on the same poster team. The art room was loud, with drums being tested next door, so most of their talking happened over paint trays. Damini asked what he listened to while painting, and next day brought a link to a song she thought he'd like. He laughed easily when the club was around, but went short when a question got personal, so she kept to posters, robotics club and the fest schedule. In the third week, with two days left, she said to the group, "A few of us are getting samosas after the last rehearsal. Come along?" Abhinav grinned. "Sure, if Rehan is coming too."

qa.q: How long before the inter-house fest did Damini and Abhinav join the poster team?
qa.a: They joined the poster team three weeks before the fest.

qa.q: What does Damini think about how comfortable Abhinav feels, and what does Damini want to avoid?
qa.a: Damini thinks Abhinav is uneasy when questions get personal, and wants to avoid pressure, so Damini keeps talk to posters, robotics club and the fest schedule.

qa.q: What alternative could Damini try if Abhinav seemed uneasy even with a group plan, and why?
qa.a: Damini could keep the friendship on projects and let Abhinav lead any next step, because comfort matters more than a quick answer.

qa.q: How might Abhinav see Damini's group invitation?
qa.a: Abhinav probably finds it relaxed and easy to accept, especially with Rehan there, so it feels like an invitation to friends and not pressure.

grounding: Over a few weeks the student chats about shared interests in projects and clubs, watching whether the other person is comfortable, before suggesting a casual group activity.

subtype: Approach: building a friendly connection first [Action]
passage: Anand had liked Gurleen since the start of Class 11, but he didn't want to be the boy who suddenly asked someone out of nowhere. So for three weeks he just talked to her like a person. They were in the same Chemistry project group, and he asked what she thought about the experiment, then actually listened. At photography club in the school's old library, he noticed she liked shooting shadows, and showed her one of his. He watched how she responded: she laughed at his jokes, started saving him a seat in the lab, sent him a photo of a cat on a scooter one Sunday. She seemed at ease. So when the club planned a photo walk in the city gardens, he said, "A few of us are going Saturday. Want to come?" "Sure," she said. "I'll bring my old camera."

qa.q: What did Gurleen like shooting at photography club?
Why did Anand wait three weeks before inviting Gurleen?
qa.a: He felt careful and a bit nervous, not wanting to make her uncomfortable by asking out of nowhere.
He built a real friendship first, watched for signs she was comfortable, and then suggested a low-pressure group outing.

qa.q: How does Gurleen seem to feel about Anand by the end?
qa.a: She seems comfortable and friendly, saving him a seat and saying yes easily to the group photo walk 🙂.

grounding: Shows a student building a friendly connection over shared projects and clubs, watching the other's comfort before suggesting a group outing.

subtype: Approach: building a friendly connection first [Action]
passage:
"You were brilliant on the motion today," Kiran said as debate club packed up.
Rehana laughed. "I lost."
"You lost well. That point about libraries, I'm stealing it."
"Steal it. I stole it from my Nani."
Over the past month they had started walking to the bus stop together after club. Kiran had noticed she stopped checking her phone when they talked about books, and that she was the one who had started saving him a spot on the steps.
"A few of us from club are going to the book fair on Sunday," Kiran said. "Imran, Tanya, me. Do you want to come along? No pressure."
Rehana thought for a second. "Can Farzana come too? She'll kill me if I go without her."
"The more the better."
"Then yes."

qa.q: Where are the club members going on Sunday?
How can you tell Rehana felt comfortable with Kiran?
qa.a: She had started saving him a spot on the steps and stopped checking her phone when they talked about books, which shows she felt at ease and interested.

qa.q: What makes Kiran's invitation a good one?
qa.a: It's a group outing with club friends and a clear "no pressure", so Rehana can join or decline easily, and bringing Farzana is welcome.

qa.q: Why might Rehana want Farzana to come too?
qa.a: Rehana may feel more relaxed with a close friend there, which keeps the outing casual.

grounding: A dialogue shows a student who built a friendship through debate club suggesting a casual group outing after seeing the other is comfortable.
